outcome: The holomorphic case was settled long before 2024 (Deligne 1974), and the open generalizations (Maass forms, GL(n) over number fields, generic temperedness for reductive groups) remain open as far as the sources show; since 26 January 2024 there are a claimed level-one Maass-form proof (Unterberger, first posted 2020, latest version February 2026, with no public expert check found), a restricted GL(3) exponent improvement (Gan, December 2025, constant unconfirmed), a trace-level 1/4 bound for ramified GL(2) over Q (Cheng, 2025), and several neighbouring or conditional results.
problem_asks: The statement names no conjecture: it says only 'a number of related conjectures that are generalizations of the original conjecture'. The original is Ramanujan's 1916 bound |tau(p)| <= 2p^(11/2) for the discriminant form. Read from the statement alone, the family it refers to has these parts: (a) Petersson's extension of the bound to holomorphic cusp forms of weight k >= 2, i.e. Hecke eigenvalues bounded by 2p^((k-1)/2) at primes not dividing the level (the holomorphic case); (b) the Maass-form version: Hecke eigenvalues of Maass cusp forms for SL(2,Z) and for congruence subgroups satisfy |lambda(p)| <= 2 at primes not dividing the level, equivalently Satake parameters have absolute value 1 (temperedness at unramified places); (c) the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GL(n) over number fields: every cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(n) is tempered at every place (unitary Satake parameters at unramified places); (d) the Howe-Piatetski-Shapiro / Shahidi generalization to connected reductive groups: each local component of a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation is tempered. The statement does not say which of (a)-(d), or any further generalization (for example the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for half-integral weight forms, or Selberg's 1/4 eigenvalue conjecture, which Langlands treats as the archimedean counterpart), is meant; the judging pass should decide. Part (a) is settled; (b), (c) and (d) are open as far as the sources show, with known exponent bounds (for example 7/64 for GL(2) over Q) and known non-tempered counterexamples for the non-generic version of (d).

events.what_happened: Deligne proves the Ramanujan bound |tau(p)| <= 2p^(11/2) and, more generally, the Ramanujan-Petersson bound for holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k >= 2, deducing it from the Weil conjectures. This is the holomorphic case. Sources: the Wikipedia article (fetched), and the Lean benchmark page for the tau case (fetched; it states the bound and shows a sorry).
events.delivers: Settles the holomorphic case (a): every holomorphic cuspidal Hecke eigenform of weight k >= 2 is tempered at every prime not dividing the level, with exponent (k-1)/2, and in particular |tau(p)| <= 2p^(11/2).
events.remains: (b) Maass forms; (c) GL(n) over number fields for n >= 2 beyond what is listed under other events; (d) general reductive groups.

checked_by.who: Pierre Deligne (author of the proof, via the Weil conjectures)
checked_by.qualification: Author of the result and of the Weil conjecture proofs it rests on
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the holomorphic bound; cited as the settled case by the Wikipedia article and by the Lean benchmark page

events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the holomorphic (settled) case; cuts toward the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Non-tempered counterexamples to the naive generalization: Kurokawa (1978) and Howe and Piatetski-Shapiro (1979) found non-tempered cuspidal representations for groups where naive temperedness fails, including Saito-Kurokawa-type lifts on Sp(4) and theta-lift constructions on unitary groups. Sources: the Wikipedia article (fetched, for the dates and the statement that the constructions are for quasi-split and split groups); Gan's lecture notes arXiv 2303.14918 (search snippet only, not opened) for the U(3) analogue.
events.delivers: Shows that the naive generalization of temperedness to all cuspidal representations of reductive groups is false. The constructions concern non-generic representations (for example CAP forms such as Saito-Kurokawa lifts). The globally generic restriction in the modern formulation of (d) is what excludes them.
events.remains: Does not decide the generic version (d) in either direction; that version is the one the modern formulation uses.

checked_by.who: Gan (lecture notes restating the Howe-Piatetski-Shapiro counterexample and its unitary analogue)
checked_by.what_they_did: Restated the counterexample and the U(3) analogue in published lecture notes; restatement, not an independent verification

events.direction: Cuts against the naive (non-generic) form of the generalization; does not touch the generic form.
events.object: Non-tempered local components realised by theta lifts: the Howe-Piatetski-Shapiro construction on Sp(4) (degree-two Siegel setting, Saito-Kurokawa lifts), and a unitary analogue on U(3) per Gan's lecture. These are explicit theta-correspondence constructions, not non-constructive existence proofs. Not opened in full.

events.what_happened: Luo, Rudnick and Sarnak give the general bound toward the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GL(n): the real parts of the Satake exponents are at most 1/2 - 1/(n^2+1). Stated for cuspidal representations of GL(n) over Q with spherical archimedean component (search snippet of the Blomer-Brumley and Gan discussions; the original paper was not opened).
events.delivers: A uniform non-sharp exponent for every n over Q (a bound toward (c), with delta = 1/2 - 1/(n^2+1)); for n = 2 it gives 3/10, weaker than the later 7/64.
events.remains: The conjecture itself (exponent 0) for every n; (b); (d).
events.direction: Bound toward the conjecture for every n; does not reach the conjectured value.

events.what_happened: Laurent Lafforgue proves the Langlands correspondence for GL(n) over global function fields (2002). The Wikipedia article and Ciubotaru-Harris (arXiv 2311.15300, opened) state that this gives temperedness, i.e. the Ramanujan bound, for cuspidal representations of GL(n) over function fields at all places.
events.delivers: Function-field analogue of (c) for GL(n): cuspidal representations are tempered at every place. This is a changed setting (function fields, not number fields) and settles nothing about number fields.
events.remains: (c) over number fields for every n; (b); (d) over number fields.

checked_by.who: Laurent Lafforgue (author); result cited as established by the Wikipedia article and by Ciubotaru-Harris
checked_by.what_they_did: Proved the function-field Langlands correspondence for GL(n)

events.direction: Analogue: cuts toward temperedness in function fields; does not cut either way for number fields.

events.what_happened: Kim and Sarnak prove the exponent 7/64 toward the Ramanujan conjecture for GL(2) over Q (Satake parameters at unramified primes satisfy p^(-7/64) <= |alpha_p| <= p^(7/64)); the proof is in Appendix 2 to H. Kim's paper in J. Amer. Math. Soc. 16 (2003) 139-183, 'Functoriality for the exterior square of GL_4 and the symmetric fourth of GL_2'. Wikipedia dates it to Kim (2002); the JAMS record gives 2003. The AMS page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; the attribution comes from search metadata.
events.delivers: A bound toward (b) for GL(2) over Q: exponent 7/64 at unramified primes (not the conjecture, which has exponent 0). It is the standing best exponent for GL(2) over Q as far as the sources read show.
events.remains: (b) exponent 0 for all Maass forms over Q; (c) for GL(n), n >= 2; (d).

checked_by.who: Journal of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal; co-author of the appendix is P. Sarnak
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper containing the appendix with the 7/64 bound

events.direction: Bound toward the conjecture for GL(2) over Q; cuts toward the conjecture without reaching it.

events.what_happened: Blomer and Brumley extend the best known bounds toward the Ramanujan conjecture for GL(n), n = 2, 3, 4, from Q to arbitrary number fields, overcoming the analytic obstacle of an infinite group of units. arXiv v1 2 March 2010; published Annals of Mathematics 174 (2011) 581-605 (AMS bibliography, search metadata).
events.revisions: v2 18 Jan 2011; v3 20 Jan 2011; v4 15 Mar 2011 (current; marked forthcoming in the Annals).
events.delivers: Pointwise bounds on Satake parameters for GL(2), GL(3), GL(4) over arbitrary number fields. The exponents are 7/64 for GL(2), 5/14 for GL(3) (both cited in Gan's paper, opened) and 9/22 for GL(4) (secondary source only). None is the conjecture (exponent 0).
events.remains: Exponent 0 for every n; (b) for number fields; (d).

checked_by.who: Annals of Mathematics (refereed journal of record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published in Ann. of Math. (2) 174 (2011), no. 1, 581-605

events.direction: Bounds toward the conjecture for n <= 4 over number fields; cuts toward it without reaching it.

events.what_happened: Shahidi (arXiv 1007.2132, July 2010; Kyoto J. Math. 51 (2011)) shows, assuming part of Arthur's A-packet conjecture, that locally generic cuspidal automorphic representations of quasi-split groups over number fields are tempered at almost all places (a 'Ramanujan type' statement). A later version states it as a consequence of Arthur's conjectures plus Clozel's generalization (search snippet, not opened).
events.revisions: Later version restates the main theorem as a consequence of the Arthur conjectures and Clozel's generalization (search snippet).
events.delivers: Conditional on part of Arthur's conjectures: temperedness at almost all places for locally generic cuspidal representations of quasi-split groups. A partial statement of (d), not a proof.
events.remains: Unconditional (d); temperedness at all places; the non-generic cases.
events.direction: Conditional partial support for (d); cuts toward the conjecture for almost all places, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Newton and Thorne prove the automorphy of symmetric power lifts Sym^n f for every n >= 1 for cuspidal level-one Hecke eigenforms, and for a broader class including forms attached to semistable elliptic curves over Q (Part I, arXiv 1912.11261, first posted 24 Dec 2019). Part II (arXiv 2009.07180, 2020) treats non-CM eigenforms. Published Publications Mathematiques de l'IHES 134 (2021), per search metadata.
events.revisions: Part I: v2 17 Jul 2020; v3 27 Sep 2021 (accepted version per comments field).
events.delivers: Functoriality (automorphy) of Sym^n for holomorphic eigenforms of level one and a broader class. The abstract does not state a Ramanujan bound for Sym^n f. Holomorphic temperedness is already settled by Deligne, so this is a neighbouring result rather than a settlement of (b), (c) or (d).
events.remains: (b) Maass forms; (c) for GL(n) over number fields beyond symmetric powers of holomorphic forms; (d).

checked_by.what_they_did: Published as Publ. Math. IHES 134 (2021), pp. 1-116 (Part I) and 117-152 (Part II), per search metadata

events.direction: Neighbouring functoriality result for symmetric powers of holomorphic forms; no direct cut toward or against the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Andre Unterberger posts 'The Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms' (arXiv 2001.10956; the title later became 'The Ramanujan-Petersson and Selberg conjectures for Maass forms'), claiming a proof, by automorphic distribution theory and pseudodifferential analysis, of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms of SL(2,Z); the abstract also says the Selberg eigenvalue conjecture for Hecke's group Gamma_0(M) follows. The current abstract (v16) still makes the SL(2,Z) claim. Sixteen versions; the latest is v16, 12 February 2026. Opened: the arXiv abstract page (version table and comment field).
events.revisions: v2 26 May 2020 (withdrawn); v3 9 Jun 2020; v4 26 Jan 2021; v5 23 Aug 2021 (withdrawn); v6 17 Sep 2021; v7 9 Jan 2022; v8 16 Feb 2022; v9 15 Jan 2024; v10 6 May 2024; v11 26 Feb 2025; v12 12 Mar 2025; v13 21 Oct 2025; v14 7 Nov 2025; v15 17 Nov 2025; v16 12 Feb 2026 (current). Comment on the current version: 'The (pseudodifferential) Section 7 has been rewritten, so as to make easier reading'.
events.delivers: As claimed: (b) for Maass forms of SL(2,Z), i.e. level one, with |lambda(p)| <= 2 at primes not dividing the level, plus the Selberg 1/4 eigenvalue conjecture for Gamma_0(M). Not established in the sense used here: no journal publication, review, or public expert verification found.
events.remains: If the claim holds: (b) for congruence subgroups other than Gamma_0(M) (scope beyond SL(2,Z) is not stated in the abstract); (c) for GL(n); (d) for general reductive groups.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 years 9 months from v1 (29 Jan 2020) to the Oct 2026 search date
events.doubts: (1) The Wikipedia article, as fetched, says the Maass version is still open ('As of 2025, ... still open'), i.e. the claim is not accepted there. (2) No journal publication, zbMATH or MathSciNet review, or expert response was found; the search tool does not index zbMATH, so this absence is not proof. (3) Versions v2 and v5 were withdrawn with no reason shown. (4) The author's companion arXiv 2004.00284 presents a parallel analytic route to the settled holomorphic case; no outside party has commented on either.

events.direction: Claims the Maass-form conjecture (|lambda(p)| <= 2 for SL(2,Z)) holds, i.e. cuts toward the conjecture for level one, if correct.

events.what_happened: Unterberger's companion preprint (arXiv 2004.00284, first posted 1 Apr 2020, titled 'A unified scheme of approach to the Ramanujan conjecture' in the version fetched; the title changes across versions). The v12 abstract does not claim the Maass case. An earlier version's abstract (search snippet, not verified) reportedly claimed the full-unimodular Maass case.

events.remains: (b) for Maass forms (not claimed in v12); (c); (d).

events.what_happened: Liyang Yang posts 'On Exceptional Maass Forms' (arXiv 2011.09054; v1 18 Nov 2020). The abstract claims to improve Kim-Sarnak's 7/64 bound toward the Satake parameters at all primes not dividing the level for exceptional Maass forms, and that the conjecture at a fixed prime for non-exceptional forms implies it for all Maass forms of that level together with Selberg's 1/4 conjecture. v2 (30 Nov 2020) is withdrawn. Comment field: 'There are typos in Lemma 8-10. Proof of Theorem B is incomplete'.
events.revisions: v2 30 Nov 2020 (withdrawn by author; the listing does not show a separate withdrawal date).
events.delivers: As claimed: an improvement of 7/64 for exceptional Maass forms only (a restricted class). The comment field states the proof of the key theorem is incomplete. Nothing is established.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, including the exceptional-form exponent.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 years (withdrawn version; no uptake found)
events.doubts: The arXiv comment field says the proof of Theorem B is incomplete and that Lemmas 8-10 have typos; the author withdrew v2.

events.what_happened: Boxer, Calegari, Gee, Newton and Thorne post 'The Ramanujan and Sato-Tate Conjectures for Bianchi modular forms' (arXiv 2309.15880, 27 Sep 2023). They prove the Ramanujan conjecture for Bianchi modular forms of weight >= 2, and more generally for regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(2) of parallel weight over any CM field. Published Forum of Mathematics, Pi 13 (2025), e10 (doi 10.1017/fmp.2024.29, per search metadata); v2 (6 Nov 2024) is the accepted version per its comment.
events.revisions: v2 6 Nov 2024 (accepted version); v3 27 Mar 2025 (version read).
events.delivers: Ramanujan bound for regular algebraic cuspidal GL(2) of parallel weight >= 2 over CM fields (including Bianchi forms over imaginary quadratic fields). A restricted case of (c) for n = 2, not Maass forms (b), not totally real fields, and not non-parallel weight.
events.remains: (b) Maass forms; (c) for GL(2) over totally real fields and for non-parallel weight, and for GL(n) with n >= 3; (d).

events.what_happened: Dan Ciubotaru and Michael Harris, 'On the generalized Ramanujan and Arthur conjectures over function fields' (arXiv 2311.15300, 26 Nov 2023; it expands and replaces arXiv 2204.06053, 2022). For a simple group G over a global function field and a cuspidal representation pi, pi_w is tempered at all unramified places where G is quasi-split, under local hypotheses at two places; there is a mild residue-cardinality restriction. The journal link annals.math.princeton.edu/articles/22237 appeared in search results and was not opened.
events.revisions: Only v1 listed on the arXiv page (opened); supersedes arXiv 2204.06053 (2022).
events.delivers: Function-field analogue of (c)/(d): temperedness at unramified places under hypotheses. It is a changed setting (function fields), so it settles nothing about number fields.
events.remains: All number-field cases of (b), (c), (d).

checked_by.qualification: Refereed journal, if the link is the publication

events.what_happened: Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu and Chi-Heng Lo post 'On the enhanced Shahidi conjecture and global applications' (arXiv 2404.05773; v1 8 Apr 2024, v2 29 Apr 2024, v3 18 Jun 2024). The abstract (fetched) gives 'the first complete proof of the enhanced Shahidi conjecture' for symplectic and split odd orthogonal groups, via intersection theory of local Arthur packets, classifies unramified representations of Arthur type (anti-generic, one local packet), and discusses global applications. A search snippet says the global consequences are conditional on the GL(n) Ramanujan conjecture; this was not confirmed in the abstract.
events.delivers: A local statement: the enhanced Shahidi conjecture for symplectic and split odd orthogonal local groups, and classification of unramified Arthur-type representations. A partial step toward (d) for those classical groups; the global consequences are not verified.
events.remains: The global temperedness statements of (d) for classical groups; (b) and (c) untouched.
events.direction: Partial local support for (d); no direct cut toward or against the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Jared Duker Lichtman and Alexandru Pascadi, 'Density theorems for GL_n via Rankin-Selberg L-functions' (arXiv 2408.13682, first posted 24 Aug 2024; v2 5 Aug 2026 adds Theorem 1.5 and referee changes, 'to appear in JEMS'). They obtain density theorems for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n over Q that fail the generalized Ramanujan conjecture at some place, improving Blomer's results near the threshold of pointwise bounds.
events.revisions: v2 5 Aug 2026 (new Theorem 1.5; to appear in JEMS per comment).
events.delivers: Density statements about how rare failures of the generalized Ramanujan conjecture at some place are, for GL_n over Q. The abstract does not claim the conjecture.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the conjecture is not proved, only the rarity of exceptions.

checked_by.who: Journal of the European Mathematical Society (referee comments, 'to appear' per v2 comment)
checked_by.what_they_did: Referee comments incorporated; listed as to appear in JEMS

events.what_happened: Yujiao Jiang, 'On Hypothesis H of Rudnick and Sarnak' (arXiv 2507.20653, 28 Jul 2025, one version, 35 pages). The abstract claims Hypothesis H in full generality for GL_n over any number field, for all n, via a stronger effective bound on Euler products with Rankin-Selberg coefficients at prime-ideal powers; it says earlier results were limited to n <= 4 by a 'functoriality barrier'. A Soochow University seminar listing (13 Oct 2025, search snippet) advertises a talk with the same title.
events.delivers: As claimed: Rudnick-Sarnak Hypothesis H (a uniform bound on local prime-power terms; the exact delta and quantity were not verified because the PDF was not readable in this session) for GL_n over number fields. A related hypothesis, not the Ramanujan-Petersson bound.
events.remains: The generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GL_n (c), (b), (d); the abstract does not say that Hypothesis H implies any Satake-parameter bound.
events.doubts: Single unrefereed preprint; no journal found by search. The proof was not read in this session (PDF unreadable). Whether Hypothesis H implies any bound on Satake parameters is not established.
events.direction: Neighbouring hypothesis; does not cut toward or against the Ramanujan conjecture on the sources read.

events.what_happened: Yuhao Cheng, 'Beyond endoscopy for GL_2 over Q with ramification 2: bounds towards the Ramanujan conjecture' (arXiv 2507.09655; v1 13 Jul 2025; v2 17 Feb 2026; v3 15 Aug 2026, the version shown). The abstract gives a new proof of the 1/4 bound toward the Ramanujan conjecture for the trace of the cuspidal part of a trace formula, for GL_2 over Q with ramification set S = {infinity, q_1, ..., q_r} containing 2, adapting Altug's unramified approach.
events.revisions: v2 17 Feb 2026; v3 15 Aug 2026 (version shown on the arXiv page).
events.delivers: A 1/4 bound for a trace (not a pointwise bound on individual Hecke eigenvalues) for ramified GL_2 over Q with 2 in S. Weaker than the 7/64 pointwise record, and restricted to ramification containing 2.
events.remains: Pointwise bounds for individual forms; ramification sets without 2; the unramified case as a pointwise statement; (b) the conjecture; (c); (d).
events.direction: Partial bound toward the conjecture at trace level for a restricted ramified class.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Pascadi and Jesse Thorner, 'Large sieves for GL_n and applications' (arXiv 2508.14888; v1 20 Aug 2025; v2 13 Sep 2025). The abstract (fetched) describes large-sieve inequalities for Satake parameters that are independent of progress toward the generalized Ramanujan conjecture; one application counts violations of that conjecture.
events.revisions: v2 13 Sep 2025 (title and abstract changed; Theorem 1.6 added).
events.delivers: Density-type bounds on the number of exceptions to the generalized Ramanujan conjecture for GL_n; does not prove any pointwise Ramanujan bound (per the abstract).
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neighbouring: bounds the number of exceptions; does not decide the conjecture.

events.what_happened: Wee Teck Gan, 'Triality and adjoint lifting for GL(3)' (arXiv 2512.08307; v1 9 Dec 2025; v2 17 Dec 2025). Using the stable twisted trace formula for the triality automorphism, lifts cuspidal GL(3) representations with a discrete-series local component to GL(8). In v2 (HTML, first 100,000 characters read), Theorem 1.4 states: for such pi over a number field k, at each unramified place the Satake eigenvalues have absolute value q_v^a with |a| <= 21/65 < 1/3, relying on Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak and improving Blomer-Brumley's 5/14. A search snippet of the v1 PDF gives the bound as 1/4 - 1/130 (Theorem 12.1); this could not be confirmed, because the v1 PDF and v1 HTML were unreadable beyond Theorems 1.2-1.3 in the introduction.
events.revisions: v1 9 Dec 2025 (abstract includes 'an application towards Ramanujan bounds for GL(3)'; the readable part of its introduction gives Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 only). v2 17 Dec 2025 (Theorem 1.4 with the bound, per the HTML). If the v1 PDF carries the bound, the first public date would be 9 Dec 2025; this could not be checked.
events.delivers: As stated in v2: a Satake exponent bound |a| <= 21/65 for cuspidal GL(3) representations with a discrete-series local component at some place, improving 5/14 for that class. Restricted by the discrete-series hypothesis; does not give exponent 0 for GL(3).
events.remains: GL(3) without the discrete-series hypothesis; the conjecture (a = 0) for GL(3); GL(n) for n >= 4; (b); (d).
events.doubts: Unrefereed. The constant conflicts between the two sources read (21/65 in v2 HTML; 1/4 - 1/130 in a search snippet of v1); see disputes. Which version carries which constant is unresolved.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture: an improved Satake exponent for a restricted GL(3) class.

events.what_happened: Dennis Gaitsgory, Vincent Lafforgue and Sam Raskin post 'Tempered vs generic automorphic functions and the canonical filtration on automorphic functions' (arXiv 2603.26925; v1 27 Mar 2026; v2 14 Apr 2026). In the everywhere-unramified function-field setting, they transfer a spectral-side filtration to automorphic functions and propose a number of conjectures tying the two filtrations; the abstract describes these as proposed conjectures. A search snippet cites an l-adic 'Ramanujan-Arthur' statement as Conjecture 3.4.6 (not verified in text).
events.delivers: Conjectures in the function-field unramified setting. The abstract establishes no temperedness statement.
events.remains: All of problem_asks in the number-field setting; the function-field conjectures remain conjectural as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: Conjectural per the abstract. Full text not read; the Conjecture 3.4.6 wording is from a search snippet only.
events.direction: Conjectural support for temperedness in the function-field setting; no direction for number fields.

events.what_happened: Sam Raskin's ICM 2026 announcement 'Conjectures of Arthur and Ramanujan for unramified automorphic forms: an announcement' (cited in arXiv 2603.26925's references; not opened, because the author's Yale-hosted PDF returned a certificate error). Raskin presented the joint work with Gaitsgory and Lafforgue at Princeton on 25 Feb 2026 (talk page opened: 'the generalized Ramanujan conjecture on automorphic forms', 'some recent progress', unramified automorphic forms over function fields, general reductive groups; the abstract does not say whether the result is proved, in preparation, or forthcoming). The announcement was posted on or before 27 Mar 2026, the date of arXiv 2603.26925, which cites it.

events.what_happened: Angdinata, Chen, Cummins and 21 co-authors (including Ken Ono), 'ABC implies that Ramanujan's tau function misses almost all primes' (arXiv 2603.29970; v1 31 Mar 2026; v2 8 Apr 2026; v3 25 Apr 2026). Assuming the abc conjecture, the number of primes l <= X that equal |tau(n)| for some n is O(X^(13/22)), so tau misses a density-one set of primes. The abstract states that the main engine was formalized and produced automatically in Lean/Mathlib by AxiomProver from a natural-language statement.

events.delivers: Conditional on abc: a density statement about which primes occur as |tau(n)|. It is a different question from the size of tau(p) or the Ramanujan-Petersson bound.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: this paper concerns the values |tau(n)|, not Hecke eigenvalue bounds.

events.what_happened: Tinghao Huang and Shifan Zhao, 'On Ramanujan Primes for Hecke-Maass Cusp Forms' (arXiv 2605.09807, single version, 10 May 2026). For a primitive Hecke-Maass form of level N, bounds the least prime p (not dividing N) at which the Ramanujan bound |lambda(p)| <= 2 holds simultaneously for two or three given forms, and lower-bounds the density of primes at which it holds for at least one form in a finite set.
events.delivers: Existence and density statements about primes at which the Ramanujan bound holds for given forms: a weaker, prime-restricted form of (b). It does not give the bound at all primes.
events.remains: The Ramanujan bound at all primes for Maass forms (b); (c); (d).
events.direction: Neighbouring: a weaker form of (b); no direction on the conjecture's truth.

events.what_happened: Jesse Jaasaari, 'On the Number of Hecke Eigenvalues of Same Sign on GL_n' (arXiv 2609.10446, 9 Sep 2026). The main result is conditional on the Generalised Ramanujan-Petersson Conjecture. Per the fetched page summary, it also proves a slightly stronger sign-count statement unconditionally for GL_2 and GL_3 forms.
events.delivers: Conditional sign-count statements for Hecke eigenvalues of self-dual Hecke-Maass forms on SL_n(Z); the unconditional part concerns sign counts for GL_2 and GL_3, not the size of the eigenvalues. Does not establish the Ramanujan bound.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.direction: Neighbouring: uses the conjecture as a hypothesis; no cut toward or against it.

Unterberger's arXiv claim (2020-2026) of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms of SL(2,Z), versus the Wikipedia article (as fetched), which describes the Maass version as still open 'as of 2025'. No refereeing or public expert verification was found.

Attribution and date of the 7/64 bound: the Wikipedia article credits Kim (2002); the JAMS record in search metadata gives Kim (2003) with Appendix 2 by Kim and Sarnak. The JAMS page was not readable (HTTP 403).

summary: Nothing in the sources read shows the generalizations of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture settled as of October 2026. The holomorphic case is settled (Deligne 1974) and is recorded as an event but is not the open part. The open parts are the Maass-form version (b), the GL(n) generalized Ramanujan conjecture over number fields (c), and generic temperedness for reductive groups (d). Since 26 January 2024 the events that move a quantity or claim a case are: (i) Gan, arXiv 2512.08307 (December 2025), a Satake exponent |a| <= 21/65 for cuspidal GL(3) representations with a discrete-series local component, improving Blomer-Brumley's 5/14 for that class according to the paper's v2 text; a search snippet gives 1/4 - 1/130 instead and I could not resolve which version carries which constant; (ii) Cheng, arXiv 2507.09655 (July 2025), a 1/4 bound for a trace in ramified GL_2 over Q with 2 in S, weaker than the pointwise 7/64 and not pointwise; (iii) Unterberger's claimed proof of the Maass-form conjecture for SL(2,Z), plus the Selberg 1/4 conjecture for Gamma_0(M), first posted January 2020 and revised through February 2026. Unterberger's claim is the close call. If correct it settles (b) at level one. I found no journal publication, review, or public expert check, the search tool does not index zbMATH so that absence is not proof, and the Wikipedia article as fetched still lists the Maass case as open. Its status should rest on what the judging pass finds in zbMATH and in any specialist report. Neighbouring events that I judge do not move the problem but that the judging pass should see: Jiang's Hypothesis H (July 2025; a related hypothesis about prime-power terms, not the Ramanujan bound); Lichtman-Pascadi (2024) and Pascadi-Thorner (2025) on the density of failures of the generalized conjecture; Huang-Zhao (2026) on primes at which the bound holds; Jaasaari (2026, conditional); Hazeltine-Liu-Lo (2024, a local result on Arthur packets for classical groups); Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin (2026) and Raskin's ICM announcement (function fields, conjectural or forthcoming); and the function-field analogues Lafforgue (2002) and Ciubotaru-Harris (2023). Boxer, Calegari, Gee, Newton and Thorne (2023, Forum Math. Pi 2025) prove the Ramanujan bound for GL(2) over CM fields with parallel weight; that predates the window and is a restricted case. On AI: no AI system is credited in any source read with a result that bears on this problem. The one AI-credited paper I opened (AxiomProver, arXiv 2603.29970, March 2026) concerns which primes arise as |tau(n)|, a different question, and is recorded as such. Searches for AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, FrontierMath/Epoch open problems, Erdos-problem AI trackers, and 'Claude/GPT/Gemini' with Ramanujan returned nothing on this conjecture. Sra's GPT-counterexample paper (arXiv 2608.29595) lists 19 counterexample entries in its repository, none described as concerning automorphic forms or Ramanujan-type bounds; the paper's PDF text was not readable, so the repository listing is the basis. The Ramanujan Challenge for AI (arXiv 2607.09721) concerns constants, not this problem. The Lean Mathlib-style benchmark page for the tau bound shows a sorry and is a statement, not a proof. The Wikipedia list entry itself (the bullet's wording in the frozen January 2024 revision) was not checked.
competing_reading: If Unterberger's SL(2,Z) argument is correct, the Maass-form part (b) is settled at level one, the Selberg Gamma_0(M) corollary follows, and the problem would move in 2020 or 2026 depending on which version is taken as the first written argument. A reader who weighs the author's repeated posting and the absence of any public objection more heavily than the absence of refereeing could count it. In the other direction, Gan's GL(3) bound moves a quantity the problem's family names (the Satake exponent) without touching the conjecture itself (exponent 0), so a reader could count a partial movement there even though the conjectured value is unchanged. And if the statement is read as only the holomorphic family (a), the problem is settled long before 2024 and nothing since matters.
what_would_settle_it: A journal acceptance or a zbMATH/MathSciNet review of arXiv 2001.10956, and a written verification or refutation of its key steps by an automorphic-forms specialist. The text of v1 and v2 of arXiv 2512.08307 to fix the GL(3) constant and the version in which it first appears. The full text of Raskin's ICM announcement and of arXiv 2603.26925 to see whether any number-field consequence is claimed. The PDF of arXiv 2507.20653 to confirm the definition of Hypothesis H and whether it yields any Satake bound. The Wikipedia list entry in its current form, to see whether the bullet has been reworded or its status changed.

incomplete: (1) The Wikipedia list entry for this bullet in the frozen January 2024 revision was not opened, so the exact bullet wording beyond the statement given was not checked. (2) The Gan GL(3) constant is unresolved: the v2 HTML gives 21/65 and a search snippet of v1 gives 1/4 - 1/130; the v1 PDF and v1 HTML were unreadable beyond the introduction's Theorems 1.2-1.3. (3) The Unterberger papers were read at the arXiv abstract and version-table level only; the full texts were not read, and no journal or zbMATH record was reachable. (4) Blomer-Brumley's main theorem and Kim's appendix were not read in text; the exponents 7/64 and 9/22 rest on secondary sources (the Wikipedia article and search snippets) and 5/14 on Gan's introduction. (5) The Raskin ICM 2026 announcement was not opened (certificate error), and the Gaitsgory-Lafforgue-Raskin conjecture numbering is from a search snippet only. (6) Jiang's Hypothesis H definition could not be read (PDF unreadable), so the claim that it is a bound on local prime-power terms and its relation to the Satake exponent is from the abstract and search snippets. (7) Sra's counterexample PDF was unreadable; the repository listing shows 19 case IDs with no automorphic entry, but the paper's own text was not checked. (8) Shahidi (2010), Lafforgue (2002), Luo-Rudnick-Sarnak (1999), Deligne (1974), and Howe-Piatetski-Shapiro (1979) were recorded from the Wikipedia article or search snippets; their original papers were not opened. (9) The 2025 Hebrew University seminar and the Soochow University seminar were seen only in search results.
